task_commit_basis: merge commit of the reference change (code after the optimization landed), from https://github.com/nestjs/nest/commit/66a76e2f04166fefc547e9db1ed74c1181248a55

reference_change.title: perf(common): faster logs by caching intl.datetimeformat

workload.source: written here from the description of https://github.com/nestjs/nest/pull/10823 (formatting the timestamp of each log line): ConsoleLogger.log called with timestamps on and stdout discarded, a fixed warm-up then a fixed window, eval/tasks/workloads/nestjs-nest-pr10823-landed/bench.ts, run through tsx

oracle.source: nest's logger.service tests (packages/common/test/services/logger.service.spec.ts), mocha-style tests run under vitest with a minimal config (eval/tasks/workloads/nestjs-nest-pr10823-landed/vitest.config.mjs); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 8x | timings: 1ms; 13ms

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. The tree's full toolchain (lerna, gulp, mocha, ts-node on a 2022 lockfile) is not installed; only what ConsoleLogger imports (reflect-metadata, rxjs, iterare, uid, tslib, uuid) at their versions before the merge, plus chai, sinon, tsx and vitest. Node is v24 from nvm. The warm-up and window counts were not chosen from a warm-up curve; the workload's direction of effect was seen once per tree
